Hello again, 

I'm interested in performing a genomic SEM factor analysis (and eventually generating summary stats).   I've identified an EFA model and would like to perform CFA (without SNPs).    Having some difficulty when attempting to run the CFA.   I checked that all of the variables in the Lavaan model are named correctly, so perhaps I'm mis-specifying the analysis?  

Any help would be appreciated,
Thanks



##  Generate covariance matrices.  
LDSCoutput <- ldsc(traits=traits, sample.prev=sample_prev, population.prev=pop_prev, ld, wld, trait.names=trait_names)
k<-nrow(LDSCoutput$S)
SE<-matrix(0, k, k)
SE[lower.tri(SE,diag=TRUE)] <-sqrt(diag(LDSCoutput$V))

# Explore the EFA 
require(Matrix)
Ssmooth<-as.matrix((nearPD(LDSCoutput$S, corr = FALSE))$mat)
require(stats)
. 


modelx <-'F1 =~ NA*PsyBIP + PsyMDD + PsySZ + PsyRiskTolerance
          F2 =~ NA*PsyOCDPGC + PsyTSYu + MedCeliacDubuois + MedTDBradfield + PsyAN + PsyADHDDemontis

          F5 =~ NA*MedTDBradfield + MedHYPO + PsyOCDPGC + MedPSCSunGu + MedVitiligoJin + PsyADHDDemontis
          F6 =~ NA*MedSLEBentham + MedPBC + MedRAOkada
          F7 =~ NA*MedCeliacDubuois + MedHYPO + PsyOCDPGC
          F1 ~~ F2 + F3 + F4 + F5 + F6 + F7
          F2 ~~ F3 + F4 + F5 + F6 + F7
          F3 ~~ F4 + F5 + F6 + F7
          F4 ~~ F5 + F6 + F7
          F5 ~~ F6 + F7
          F6 ~~ F7'

model_out<-usermodel(covstruc = LDSCoutput,
           estimation = "DWLS",
            model = modelx,
            CFIcalc = TRUE,

Hi Dan,

Based on the error it looks like the "fake" model used to determine ordering of the sampling covariance matrix used for CFI estimation wasn't converging. I've added in code to force that fake model to converge if you want to re-install Genomic SEM and restart R and give it a try. 

It sounds like for previous runs you were excluding certain variables entirely based on the loadings? I ask largely because that would explain why the error you posted wasn't coming up in those cases. As far as recommendations for picking up loadings, it's really hard to give a rule of thumb on that end. I think it can kind of depend how much your variables generally hang together, so if you've got a lot of variables with loadings of > .5 and one or two loners of < .2 then you might make a different judgement call about cut-offs then if you have a set of variables all with loadings of ~.3. With that said, I've used a cut-off of .35 in my most recent project. 

-Andrew
